title: Look for corroboration
odia:
ଏକା ଆଖି ଆଖି ନୁହଁ
ଏକା ସାକ୍ଷୀ ସାକ୍ଷୀ ନୁହଁ।
literal_meaning: A single eye is no eye; a single witness is no witness.
meaning_odia: ଜଣକର କଥା ଶୁଣି ନିଷ୍ପତ୍ତି ନେବା ପୂର୍ବରୁ ଅନ୍ୟ ସମର୍ଥନ ବା ପ୍ରମାଣ ଖୋଜିବାର ସତର୍କତା ଭାବେ କଥାଟିକୁ ଏଠାରେ ପଢ଼ାଯାଇଛି। ଆଖି ଓ ସାକ୍ଷୀର ତୁଳନାଟି ଏହି ପ୍ରବଚନର ଜୋରଦାର କଥନ।
explanation: The two lines repeat the same pattern: one alone is declared insufficient. This edition reads the witness comparison as a call to seek corroboration before settling a disputed account. Its emphatic wording belongs to the proverb; it is neither a rule of law nor a factual assessment of people who see with one eye.
usage_example: Two friends hear one account of a disagreement and decide to ask what else happened before taking sides. One might recall this saying as a reminder to check the account. This illustration is newly composed.
cultural_context: ଏକା begins each line, and the repeated noun is followed by ନୁହଁ, creating a parallel denial. The verse moves from an image of seeing to the act of bearing witness, making corroboration its central concern in this reading.
